title: A 2025 review says older infants pick up action contingencies faster
summary: Cuevas and Colombo's 2025 review says older infants acquire operant contingencies more rapidly than younger infants.
body: Cuevas and Colombo, reviewing infant contingency learning, say decades of work found that even very young infants learn response-reinforcement contingencies. They also say the work found an age change: older infants acquire operant contingencies more rapidly than younger infants. They cite Davis and Rovee-Collier (1983) among others. This card did not open those studies. It records the review's summary, not a new count.

sources.title: A quarter century of research on infant contingency learning: current and future directions
sources.author: Kimberly Cuevas and John Colombo
sources.note: Supports the review's statement that older infants acquire operant contingencies more rapidly than younger infants. Infant Behavior and Development 2025;80:102068.
